characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Ultra55 scanning electron microscope; specimens prepared by vibration polishing with 50 nm colloidal silica for 2.5–24 h in a Buehler-VibroMet 2
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fully recrystallized single equiaxed FCC γ phase with high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries and no B2 phase; average grain size excluding twins 7.63 μm, including twins 3.51 μm; no strong texture
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: IPF and phase maps; 20 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Reveal grain structure, phase constitution and grain size of the UFCed 3Cr steel

characterization_methods.key_findings: Only five FCC austenite reflections γ(111), γ(200), γ(220), γ(311), γ(222); no B2/BCC reflection — confirms single-phase FCC γ austenite

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 operating at 200 kV; specimens prepared by EDM, ground to <80 μm, thinned with Struers TenuPol-3 (10 vol% perchloric acid + 90 vol% ethanol, 20 V, −30 °C)
characterization_methods.key_findings: γ grains with annealing twins, dislocation lines and stacking-fault-like fringes; microstructure all γ austenite
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: along [011]γ zone axis; 1 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm the γ austenite microstructure of the 3Cr steel

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 at 200 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: Very fine, faintly bright ordered domains (LRO domains) homogeneously dispersed in the γ matrix; the smallest of the four steels
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: DF taken from a {110} LRO-type reflection; 20 nm scale bar
characterization_methods.purpose: Image the ordered LRO domains in the 3Cr steel

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI Tecnai G2 F20 at 200 kV
characterization_methods.key_findings: Very faint superlattice reflections at 1/2{0-22}γ and/or 1/2{200}γ positions but no satellite spots around γ reflections, indicating formation of LRO domains (not κ'-carbides) in the UFCed 3Cr steel; primary γ spots 000γ, 111γ, 100γ with weak 100LRO/011LRO superlattice spots
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the ordered structure in the 3Cr steel

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HRTEM along [011]γ zone axis; IFFT reconstructed using {011} and {100} superlattice reflections
characterization_methods.key_findings: LRO domains are ellipsoidal with interconnected morphology typical of spinodal decomposition; average size ~1.75 nm for the 3Cr steel (measured over >200 domains by Image-Pro Plus)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 10 nm scale bars; FFT insets labelled 000, 111γ, 200γ, 100LRO, 011LRO
characterization_methods.purpose: Resolve the LRO domains at atomic scale and measure their size

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM; secondary-electron images; 200 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dimpled microvoid-coalescence morphology with fine tear ridges and several larger deep circular holes plus a coarser elongated void region; ductile fracture mode
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: fibre zone of the fracture surface plus macroscopic fracture surface inset
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the fracture mode of the 3Cr steel

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Crystal structures considered: disordered γ, ordered γ (L12), κ-carbide (E21, (Fe,Mn)3AlC), AlNi3C, Cr21(FeC3)2, Fe2NiC
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: DFT with generalized gradient approximation (GGA) and Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) functional
computational_details.simulation_method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculation of formation energies of possible (κ-)carbide structures in Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C steel
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated formation energies used to rationalize the observed κ-carbide/LRO domain size trend (Ni promotes, Cr suppresses) observed by TEM/DF for the 3Cr steel

analytical_models.equation_role: σys = σ0 + σss + σgb + σprep; dislocation strengthening neglected for fully recrystallized Fe–Mn–Al–C steel
analytical_models.model_note: σ0 = 3τ0 with τ0 = 2×10^-4 G; with G = 70 GPa, σ0 = 42 MPa
d_eff values from EBSD: 3.51, 3.73, 3.72, 2.2 μm for 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr; calculated σgb = 238.5, 231.3, 231.7, 301.2 MPa respectively
Computed σss for 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr = 515.4, 509.5, 557.2, 554.1 MPa respectively; bracket terms are wt% of dissolved elements
For 3Cr, σ_order also contributes because some LRO nanodomains are smaller than the critical size; σ_order bars span ~0.5–1.0 nm with peak approaching ~15 MPa

analytical_models.model_name: Precipitation strengthening — coherency + modulus mismatch (Equations 3 and 4)
analytical_models.model_note: σprep taken as the larger of σ_order and σcoh+σmod; for the 3Cr steel σcoh+σmod is dominant (orange bars span ~1.0–2.3 nm, tallest near 15 MPa)

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical yield-strength superposition model (linear combination of strengthening mechanisms)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated total yield-strength contributions are compared with the measured yield strengths in Fig. 11; experimental values exceed the summed calculated contributions for all samples

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation slip constrained within planar slip bands; dislocation multipoles localized within {111} slip bands
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: At 3% strain, [011](1-11) slip system Schmid factor 0.52; dislocation multipoles localized within {111} slip bands, dislocations constrained within planar (1-11) slip bands and interacting (1-11)/(11-1) slip bands.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: high-density dislocation arrays (HDDA) restricted by intersecting planar slip bands; dynamic slip band refinement (DSBR)
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: At 10% strain, slip-band spacing narrows, slip-band number increases, dislocation density increases; (1-11) and (11-1) slip bands carry high-density dislocation arrays (HDDA) restricted by the (1-11) and (11-1) planar slip bands.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: deformation twinning and stacking faults near fracture
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: At ~54% strain (LD), nanometre-width deformation twins and dozens of nanometre-width stacking faults observed; twins appear only near the fracture surfaces so their contribution to overall ductility/strain hardening is expected to be very limited; 3Cr steel deformation dominated by HDDA and dislocation slip with strain hardenability mainly from HDDA densification and DSBR.

interfaces.interface_notes: The 3Cr steel (x=0 Ni, y=3 Cr) contains LRO domains rather than κ-carbides; κ-carbide/LRO domain size decreases with increasing Cr content (largest in 2Ni, smallest in 3Cr).
interfaces.phase_evolution: No B2/second phase in the as-processed state; Cr addition suppresses κ-carbide formation and, at high Cr content, stabilizes LRO domains instead of κ-carbides; the 3Cr steel forms LRO domains homogeneously distributed in the γ matrix.

phase_interfaces.coherence: coherent (faint superlattice reflections at 1/2{0-22}γ and/or 1/2{200}γ; interconnected spinodal-like morphology)

interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar dislocation slip dominates the whole deformation of 3Cr steel: at 3% strain planar slip bands/multipoles; at 10% strain (1-11) and (11-1) intersecting planar slip bands with HDDA; at ~54% (LD) high-density dislocations, very fine slip bands, nanometre-width deformation twins and stacking faults.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: yield strength (comparison between 3Cr and higher-Ni 2Ni3Cr steel with equivalent grain size)
TS × TEL = 62.07 GPa-% (product of tensile strength and total elongation) placing it above literature Fe-Al, Fe-Mn, Fe-Mn-C, Fe-Mn-Al-C, 301LN and 304 stainless steels in the YS vs TS×TEL plot

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Four ingots with nominal compositions Fe–20Mn–9Al-1.5C-xNi-yCr (x = 0, 2 wt%, y = 0, 3, 5 wt%) prepared by vacuum induction melting under high-purity Ar; the 3Cr ingot corresponds to x=0, y=3.
As-cast ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h.
Ingots were hot-rolled to 4 mm-thick sheets with 95% thickness reduction; initial rolling temperature 1040–1060 °C and finishing temperature 950–970 °C.
Plate was online ultrafast cooled to ambient temperature at ~40 °C/s using the in-house ADCOS-PM device.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Interrupted tensile tests to engineering strains of 3% (or 5%) and 10% were also performed
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: EDM-cut tensile specimens along rolling direction (RD), gauge length 25 mm, thickness 3 mm, width 7 mm; laser extensometer to monitor strain; at least three specimens

strain_hardening_rate.value: 3Cr strain-hardening curve shows a sharp minimum at low strain, a maximum just above 2000 MPa near true strain 0.2–0.25, then decline to zero shortly before true strain 0.4; three stages I, II, III identified

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering and true stress–strain curves for 3Cr shown in Fig. 4a and Fig. 4b; 3Cr (black curve) shows the longest elongation (~0.55 engineering strain) with a lower flow plateau near 1100 MPa, reaching the highest true stresses (~1600–1800 MPa band) at the largest strains

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: SEM fractography of the fibre zone and macroscopic fracture surface

average_grain_size.value: 7.63 μm (excluding twin boundaries); 3.51 μm (including twin boundaries)

grain_structure.texture: no strong texture observed in EBSD IPF map

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries
ellipsoidal, spatially localized domains with interconnected morphology typical of spinodal decomposition, homogeneously distributed in the γ matrix
phases_present.phase_name: long-range ordered (LRO) domains / ordered γ (E21-related superlattice)
phases_present.volume_fraction: very low (superlattice diffraction intensity low; quantitative estimate not possible from DF)

precipitates.coherency: coherent with the γ austenite matrix (faint superlattice reflections at 1/2{0-22}γ and/or 1/2{200}γ positions)
precipitates.distribution: homogeneously distributed in the γ matrix
precipitates.type: LRO nanodomains (ordered domains; the 3Cr steel forms LRO domains rather than κ-carbides)

structures.overall_structure: Single equiaxed face-centred cubic (FCC) γ austenite phase, fully recrystallized, with a high fraction of Σ3 twin boundaries; no B2 (BCC) phase detected by EBSD or XRD.

unmapped_findings: The UFCed 3Cr steel (Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-3Cr; measured composition C 1.31, Si 0.36, Mn 20.1, P 0.011, S 0.002, Al 8.21, Mo 0.51, Ni 0.18, Cr 2.88, Ti 0.01, Nb 0.03, Fe Bal. wt.%) has the highest total elongation (54.4%) among the four steels of the study but the lowest yield strength (969 MPa) and tensile strength (1141 MPa).

3Cr steel forms nanoscale long-range-ordering (LRO) domains instead of κ-carbides because of its high Cr content; Cr increases the κ-carbide formation energy and nucleation barrier, suppressing κ-carbide growth.

For the 3Cr steel the calculated formation energy of the Cr-rich carbide Cr21(FeC3)2 is −0.049 eV/atom (favourable but 0.111 eV/atom higher than the ideal κ-carbide (Fe,Mn)3AlC at −0.160 eV/atom), increasing the nucleation energy barrier.
Product of tensile strength and total elongation for the 3Cr steel is TS × TEL = 62.07 GPa-%, the highest among the four present steels (Table 2).

3Cr steel strain hardenability is mainly contributed by HDDA densification and dynamic slip band refinement (DSBR); deformation twins and stacking faults appear only near the fracture surfaces at very high strain (~54%, LD) and contribute very limited overall ductility.

For the 3Cr steel, the strengthening contributions calculated are σ0 = 42 MPa, σgb = 238.5 MPa and σss = 515.4 MPa, with precipitation strengthening (σcoh+σmod dominant, plus a non-negligible σ_order contribution) completing the σys superposition; experimental YS exceeds the summed calculated contributions (Fig. 11).
